clue.text: Play safe with hammer

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer might hammer a show

explanation.surface: Someone is told to crack open a safe with a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is underworld slang for a safe, and to pan or hammer something is to slate it.
explanation.definitionFit: J M Barrie's famous stage drama about the boy who never grew up.

clue.text: Horse-drawn carriage that's turned up conveying queen and attendant

indicators.note: conveying means carrying, so the reversed pair holds the queen abbreviation
in a down clue, turned up means these letters are written bottom to top

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is'
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage arrives bearing the queen and her attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is i.e., and 'turned up' in a down clue flips it before it is wrapped round the queen; 'conveying' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An equipage is a carriage with its horses and liveried servants, a grand horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Crowd aboard more popular form of transport

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the crowd word sits within the word for more

parts.note: extra means more, additional
to press is a crowd, as the press of people
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A crowd climbs aboard a more popular means of travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast train stopping at few stations is a kind of rail transport.

clue.text: Place to live, one incorporating everything by old Italian architect

indicators.note: incorporating means taking in, so the home-and-one letters wrap round the word for everything

parts.note: a pad is informal for a flat or home
all means everything
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A house built by an old Italian architect has room for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just links; 'old' looks like part of the description of the architect but gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Palladio was the sixteenth-century Venetian designer whose villas inspired Palladian style.

clue.text: Single fellow rising above endless prejudice in part of Africa

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single
a man is a fellow

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: bias means prejudice

explanation.surface: A lone man rises above prejudice somewhere in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the single fellow in a down clue; 'endless' docks the prejudice word, and 'above' is just the down-clue position.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-western Africa.

clue.text: Offer to wrap dress for woman

indicators.note: to wrap means to go round, so the offer word encloses the dress word

parts.note: to bid is to make an offer
rig means clothing, outfit

explanation.surface: Someone offers to wrap a dress up for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigid is a female given name, as of the Irish saint.

clue.text: Army cook snubs fine foreign food

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

indicators.note: to snub originally means to cut short, so the word for cook is docked of the word for fine

parts.note: taken as written
OK means fine

explanation.surface: An army cook turns his nose up at fine foreign cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snubs' is used in its old sense of docking or cutting short; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: A taco is a Mexican folded tortilla with a filling, a dish from abroad.

clue.text: Help for a calculating sort, I guess

definitions.text: Help for a calculating sort, I guess

parts.words: Help for a calculating sort, I guess
parts.note: a ready-made table helps anyone working out sums, and the word also suggests one who says 'I reckon', I guess

explanation.definitionFit: A ready table of computed figures aids calculation; the word also names one who reckons or estimates.

clue.text: Dog mated after lead removed? Trouble said to follow

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: paired means mated, as birds do

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A dog was mated once its lead was taken off, and trouble followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead removed' strips the first letter of the mated word; 'said' turns trouble into a sound-alike drink, and 'to follow' places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is a large terrier breed from Yorkshire.

clue.text: Quickly swallow piece of cake that's been passed round

indicators.note: passed round means turned about, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a plug is a piece cut from a cake of compressed tobacco

explanation.surface: Someone gobbles a slice of cake that is being handed round.
explanation.definitionFit: To gulp is to swallow hastily in large mouthfuls.

clue.text: Railway wagons loaded with animals

parts.note: rolling, as in rolling in it, means loaded with money
stock means livestock, farm animals

explanation.surface: Railway wagons are packed full with livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling stock is the collective term for a railway's carriages and trucks.

clue.text: In Paris these supply opportunities to learn new trade

indicators.note: supply read as supple, bending flexibly, signals the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: French schemes offer people the chance to train in a new line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as an adverb, supplely, bending the letters of IN PARIS THESE into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Traineeships are training posts in which people learn a job.

clue.text: Chose not to bid spades, after wavering

indicators.note: wavering means unsteady, so the letters shift about

explanation.surface: A bridge player, having wobbled, declines to bid in spades.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, saying 'pass' is declining to make a bid.

clue.text: Trader in costume jewellery that's reduced by 25%

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: losing a quarter of an eight-letter word leaves its first three quarters, six letters

parts.note: diamante is sparkling fake jewellery

explanation.surface: A trader deals in costume jewellery that is marked down by a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: DIAMANTE has eight letters; keeping three quarters leaves its first six.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant ship trading with India, such as an East India Company vessel.

clue.text: Not needing soldiers, discharge military unit

indicators.note: not needing means doing without, so the soldiers' letters are left out

parts.note: a secretion is a discharge from the body
RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: With no need for troops, a military unit is discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: SECRETION loses RE, the Royal Engineers, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a small subdivision of a platoon in the army.

clue.text: Photograph striker's hopeful effort

definitions.meaning: a quick informal picture taken with a camera
in football, a ... is a quick speculative strike at goal

explanation.definitionFit: A casual photo is a snapshot; a footballer's quick hit at goal is a snap shot.

clue.text: Flying about in jet or plane

indicators.note: about means around, so the mixed letters go round the small word
flying suggests the letters scattering through the air

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flies about in a jet or other aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: JET OR rearranged as JOTER goes about IN. 'plane' is not an aircraft but the woodworking tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A jointer is a long carpenter's plane for truing edges of boards.

clue.text: Said to be most prolific author without qualifications?

indicators.note: said to be means spoken, a word sounding like another

parts.note: the most prolific author would outwrite every rival

explanation.surface: Who is the most prolific author, and does he lack any qualifications?
explanation.walkthrough: The 'author' sense is a whimsical one: to outwrite everyone is what the top producer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Outright means completely, with no reservations or conditions.

clue.text: Arrested by the Old Bill, yours truly's given the third degree

parts.note: ex means former, old

indicators.note: arrested by means held by, so the possessive word sits within the others

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
yours truly is the speaker, and the speaker's is mine

explanation.surface: Picked up by the police, I've been questioned brutally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Old Bill' is British slang for the police, a false trail: 'Old' and 'Bill' work separately, and 'Arrested by' puts the possessive inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone the third degree is to question them closely, to interrogate.

clue.text: Crates of explosives?

parts.note: crates are old cars, slang ..., and explosive fireworks are also called ...

explanation.definitionFit: Bangers are both decrepit cars and loud fireworks, so the clue fits both senses.

clue.text: Palace supporter after end of match caught in a strike

indicators.note: after means the supporter comes at the end
caught in means trapped inside, so the final letter sits within the strike word

parts.note: to lam is to beat or strike

indicators.note: end of means the last letter is taken

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A Crystal Palace supporter, after a match, is caught in a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palace' suggests Crystal Palace football club; 'end of' takes the last letter of match, 'caught in' puts it in the strike word, 'after' sends the supporter last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress at Granada in Spain.

clue.text: My book: An Englishman Abroad?

parts.note: limey is American slang for a Briton, as he is called abroad

explanation.surface: An author names his book after a famous play about an Englishman overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An Englishman Abroad' is the title of an Alan Bennett play, but here it is just a description.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My!' and this British cry are both exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Old citizen ultimately content with abolition of explosive substance

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
a ban is a prohibition, an abolition

explanation.surface: A veteran citizen is happy to see an explosive outlawed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Theban was a citizen of ancient Thebes in Greece or Egypt.

clue.text: High Church maintains religious instruction is worth a lot

indicators.note: maintains means holds up, so the church letters stand after the instruction letters as support

parts.note: high means smelly, stinking, as of meat gone off
RI is the abbreviation for religious instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A High Church keeps up religious teaching, which is very valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High Church' looks like one phrase; 'High' is STINKING and 'Church' is CH. RI, religious instruction, is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Being extremely wealthy means having a great fortune, an informal intensifier phrase.

clue.text: Thought middleman oddly absent

indicators.note: with the odd-placed letters gone, only the even ones remain

explanation.surface: A thought: the middleman is strangely not around.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a notion or something thought up.

clue.text: Heading west, a small number reach island, one in Inner Hebrides

indicators.note: in an across clue heading west means reading right to left

parts.note: no., shortened, is an abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A small group sails west and reaches an island in the Hebrides.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus NO heading west gives ONA, which reaches I for island; 'reach' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small isle off Mull, famous for St Columba's abbey.

clue.text: Soldiers must accept awfully severe gaffer

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the soldiers' letters enclose the rest

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: awfully means badly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The troops have to put up with a terribly harsh boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles severe, and 'must accept' has the soldiers' letters take that jumble in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffer is a foreman or boss, someone who supervises workers.

clue.text: Reserve ready to join Ist XI?

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go
a 1st XI is a team's first eleven, its A side

explanation.surface: A reserve player is ready to join the first eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ist' is the printed 1st; an XI is a cricket or football team of eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: To set aside something is to keep it back for later, to reserve it.
